section_path: 2.4 Common Vibration Severity Charts and Tables
generated_text: This chart, based on VDI 2056 and ISO 2372 standards, categorizes machine vibration severity using RMS velocity (mm/s) into four zones (A, B, C, D) for different classes of machines (Class I, II, III, IV). Each zone indicates a specific condition, from good to not permissible, depending on the machine type and its foundation.

groups.name: Class I
groups.machine_description: Individual parts of engines and machines, integrally connected with the complete machine in its normal operating condition. (production electrical motors of up to 15 kW are typical examples of machines in this category).

groups.name: Class II
groups.machine_description: Medium sized machines, (typically electrical motors with 15 to 75 kW output) without special foundations, rigidly mounted engines or machines (up to 300 kW) on special foundation.

groups.name: Class III
groups.machine_description: Large prime movers and other large machines with rotating masses mounted on rigid and heavy foundations which are relatively stiff in the direction of vibration measurement.

groups.name: Class IV
groups.machine_description: Large prime movers and other large machines with rotating masses mounted on rigid and heavy foundations which are relatively soft in the direction of vibration measurement.
